title: Geometric irreducibility is preserved by subalgebras and directed colimits
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A commutative $k$-algebra means a commutative unital ring $A$ with a fixed unital homomorphism $k\to A$; it is called geometrically irreducible when the associated $k$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-scheme-over-base] is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. (1) Let $A,S$ be commutative $k$-algebras and $u:A\to S$ an injective unital ring homomorphism commuting with the maps from $k$. If $S$ is geometrically irreducible, then $A$ is geometrically irreducible. (2) Let $I$ be a nonempty small directed poset (every two elements have a common upper bound) and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of commutative $k$-algebras with transition maps preserving $k$. If each $A_i$ is geometrically irreducible, then its colimit $\varinjlim_i A_i$ in commutative $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is geometrically irreducible. Transition maps need not be injective. No finite-generation or reducedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 037N, lemma-subalgebra-geometrically-irreducible, assertions (1) and (3), lines 11235--11257; (1) written for an injective k-algebra map via its image

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary field extension $K/k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(T\otimes_kK)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $T$. Thus [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] reduces each assertion to irreducibility of these spectra for every $K$. We will use [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime]: this is exactly properness and primality of the ideal of nilpotent elements. In particular every algebra assumed geometrically irreducible has nonzero tensor product with $K$.

source.place: Tag 037N, reduction to arbitrary field extension; definition-geometrically-irreducible immediately before it; Tag 00ES(2).

proof.text: For assertion (1), $K$ is a flat $k$-module. Indeed apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] with $D=k$; [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] implies flatness of $k\otimes_kK$. The maps $k\otimes_kK\to K$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, and $K\to k\otimes_kK$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, are inverse $k$-linear maps by bilinearity, so flatness transfers to $K$. Since $u$ is injective and $k$-linear, [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] gives an injection $v=u\otimes1:A\otimes_kK\to S\otimes_kK$. Its multiplicativity and preservation of $1$ follow on pure tensors from [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and extend by generation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 037N proof, first sentence (tensoring the injection); Tag 00HD definition of flatness.

proof.text: Write $B=A\otimes_kK$ and $C=S\otimes_kK$. Injectivity gives $x^n=0$ in $B$ if and only if $v(x)^n=0$ in $C$. Hence $N_B=v^{-1}(N_C)$. By [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime] and the hypothesis on $S$, $N_C$ is prime and proper. Its inverse image is proper since $v(1)=1\notin N_C$; if $xy\in N_B$, then $v(x)v(y)\in N_C$, so $v(x)\in N_C$ or $v(y)\in N_C$, hence $x\in N_B$ or $y\in N_B$. The same criterion gives irreducibility of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Since $K/k$ was arbitrary, [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and the identification in step 1 prove (1).

source.place: Tag 037N proof, subalgebra assertion; equivalent nilradical formulation of the irreducibility argument, Tag 00ES(2).

proof.text: For assertion (2), let $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ with maps $\iota_i$. Regard the given nonempty small directed poset as a small filtered category: it has a common target for any two objects, and parallel arrows are equal. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise], $A$ is a colimit of the underlying rings and every element has a representative $\iota_i(a)$. It is also a colimit of the underlying $k$-modules, as follows directly. For any compatible family of $k$-linear maps $f_i:A_i\to M$, put $f(\iota_i(a))=f_i(a)$. This is independent of the representative by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero]: equality is witnessed at a common later stage. To check additivity, move two representatives to a common upper bound and use additivity there; scalar compatibility is checked at a single stage. Every element has a representative, so $f$ is the unique such linear map. This proves the required module colimit universal property.

source.place: Tag 037N proof, final sentence; underlying colimit description as in Tags 00D6 and 00D7.

proof.text: Put $B_i=A_i\otimes_kK$ and $B=A\otimes_kK$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits] to the small diagram of $k$-modules of step 4, with $N=K$. It says that $B$, with maps $j_i=\iota_i\otimes1$, is the module colimit of the $B_i$. The maps $j_i$ and all transition maps are unital ring maps: on pure tensors they preserve $1\otimes1$ and the multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a\prime\otimes b\prime)=aa\prime\otimes bb\prime$ of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]; bilinearity and generation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extend the identity. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], every element of $B$ is represented in some $B_i$, two such representatives can be moved to a common stage, and an element maps to zero precisely when it becomes zero at a later stage. These facts require no injectivity of transition maps.

source.place: Tag 037N proof, final sentence; tensor commutation Tag 00DD and module colimit descriptions Tags 00D6, 00D7.

proof.text: Each $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is irreducible by the hypotheses and step 1, so [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime] says $N_{B_i}$ is proper and prime. Choose $i\in I$, possible by nonemptiness. If $1_B=0$, then $j_i(1_{B_i})=0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] gives some $j\geq i$ where the image of $1_{B_i}$ is zero. The transition map is unital, so $1_{B_j}=0$, contrary to properness of $N_{B_j}$. Thus $1_B\ne0$ and $N_B$ is proper: $1_B$ cannot be nilpotent.

source.place: Tag 037N(3), nonemptiness implicit in irreducibility; final proof sentence expanded using Tag 00D7.

proof.text: To prove primality of $N_B$, take $x,y\in B$ with $xy\in N_B$, and choose $n\geq1$ with $(xy)^n=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] and directedness, represent $x,y$ in one $B_i$ by $x_i,y_i$. Since the coprojections preserve products, $j_i((x_iy_i)^n)=0$. The same cited zero criterion gives $j\geq i$ where $(x_jy_j)^n=0$. The prime ideal $N_{B_j}$ of step 6 therefore contains $x_j$ or $y_j$. Some positive power of the corresponding element is zero at stage $j$, and its image in $B$ has that same power zero. Consequently $x\in N_B$ or $y\in N_B$. Together with step 6 this makes $N_B$ prime. By [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime], $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is irreducible. This holds for every $K/k$, so [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and step 1 give (2). No finite-generation or reducedness was used.

source.place: Tag 037N(3), final proof sentence expanded by detection of one nilpotence relation at a finite stage; Tag 00ES(2).

proof_origin.place: Expansion of Tag 037N(1),(3), following its tensor/base-change reduction, with the equivalent nilradical criterion of Tag 00ES(2) replacing its minimal-prime/image argument in (1) and spelling out the directed-colimit argument in (3).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-5c0ff7332 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 7 steps, the new leaf, the statement of every cited node, Stacks algebra.tex 11207-11257 (Definition 037M, Lemma 037N and its proof), blueprint main-20261015 lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve proof paragraph 3, and Mathlib RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Topology.lean:276. Statement: it matches 037N(1) (injective k-map, equivalent via the image) and 037N(3). Requiring I to be nonempty adds nothing, since the empty colimit would be k, which is geometrically irreducible. Nothing is weakened, no hypothesis is added, and it matches both uses in the citer lem-zl-generic-point-geometric-irreducibility. Step 1: the fibre-product leaf identifies the base change with Spec(T⊗K), which bridges the DAG definition and Stacks 037M. Steps 2-3: K is flat via the faithfully-flat leaf with D=k and k⊗K≅K. The injective tensor map is a unital ring map, and the preimage of a proper prime nilradical is a proper prime nilradical. Step 4 constructs the module-colimit universal property instead of claiming it from a node: well-definedness via the rings-zero leaf, k-linearity because the ι_i are algebra maps, uniqueness via representatives. Step 5: tensor commutes with colimits, and the modules-elementwise leaf needs no injectivity. Step 6: nonemptiness of I gives 1≠0 in B. Step 7: finite-stage detection of (xy)^n=0 plus primality at stage j proves the nilradical of B is prime. All 12 proof dependencies are Mathlib leaves, so there is no route issue. The declared tool_uses are harmless and accepted but unnecessary. New node lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime: an exact one-line specialization of PrimeSpectrum.irreducibleSpace_iff_isPrime_nilradical (CommSemiring version; IrreducibleSpace includes nonempty, IsPrime includes proper). It is self-contained, has three kinds of search and correct blueprint.from/via, and is not a restatement of an item clause. Tested on the zero ring, a field, the dual numbers, k×k and k[x,y]/(xy). The rg duplicate search (nilradical, 00ES, the declaration name, geometrically irreducible) found no duplicate; lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes and lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible do not state the criterion. No SGA cited. No changes made.
